input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator logic was inverted during the refactor. The original code was `("; " if any_prefix_is_slash else " / ").join(rv)`, but the new code is `("; " if not any_prefix_is_slash else " / ").join(rv)`.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with both primary and secondary opts, such as `--flag/--no-flag`. Before the change, the separator was " / " when no slash prefix was used, and "; " when a slash prefix was used. Now it is "; " for ordinary options and " / " for slash-prefixed ones. Help output changes from `--shout / --no-shout` to `--shout; --no-shout`, and slash-prefix options also get the wrong separator.
critique: The finding points to the same negated any_prefix_is_slash condition in the separator selection. It describes the same effect: ordinary flags get '; ' and slash-prefixed options get ' / ', with the '--shout; --no-shout' example.
